name: Roswell UFO Incident Theories
claim: Debris recovered near Roswell in July 1947 was an alien craft, with bodies recovered and concealed.
description: The Army first announced a 'flying disc', then a weather balloon. The 1994 Air Force report identified the debris as Project Mogul — a classified balloon array for detecting Soviet nuclear tests — and 'bodies' as later anthropomorphic test dummies. The incident, revived by ufologists in the late 1970s, remains the anchor of UFO conspiracy culture.

name: Area 51 Alien Technology
claim: The Groom Lake facility houses recovered alien craft that are being reverse-engineered.
description: The secrecy is real — Area 51 developed the U-2, A-12/SR-71, and stealth aircraft, and the CIA only acknowledged the base in 2013 — which explains decades of unexplained sightings. Bob Lazar's 1989 claims of working on alien propulsion made the base world-famous; no physical evidence has ever corroborated the alien component.

name: Majestic 12
claim: A secret committee of twelve scientists and officials, formed by Truman in 1947, manages UFO crash retrievals.
description: Rests on documents mailed anonymously on film to a UFO researcher in 1984. The FBI declared them 'completely bogus'; internal anachronisms (format, typeface, an incorrect Truman signature lifted from another letter) mark them as forgeries. MJ-12 nonetheless became load-bearing lore for later UFO claims.

name: Crop Circle Theories
claim: Crop formations are made by alien craft or unknown energies.
description: Doug Bower and Dave Chorley demonstrated in 1991 how they had made hundreds with planks and rope since 1976; circle-making teams now produce openly commissioned formations of great complexity. Residual claims focus on formations asserted to be too intricate — an unfalsifiable remainder.
